How to play: Choose a project and a number of processors, then use the arrows to reorder the priority list.

Priority list (earlier tasks are chosen first)

Schedule

Look for the math

A project can never finish sooner than its longest chain of tasks. That chain is the key to both planning and checking a schedule.

The critical path

Add the durations along each route from Start to End. The longest total is the critical path, and it is a lower bound on the finishing time. Tasks on it have zero slack: a delay to any of them delays the whole project. Tasks off it have spare time, computed from the difference between their earliest and latest starts.

List scheduling

A priority list decides which ready task goes to a free processor. Changing the list can change the finishing time even though the precedence rules stay fixed. The logic test checks on three projects that every schedule respects precedence, never runs two tasks on one processor, and never beats the critical path; with enough processors it reaches that lower bound exactly.

Move a long task to the top of the priority list. Does the schedule get shorter?
